_about: Children of God side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of being God's children that more than one book shares, from Exodus and the prophets to the Gospels and the letters, each said to those its verse names, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme's own outline cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: Children of God

Gospels & Acts: He gave the right to become children of God
The letters: the glorious freedom of the children of God
it is not the children of the flesh who are God's children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring
that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are!
we are now children of God
we love the children of God
the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil

rows.alike: John and the letters use the same words, "children of God": "He gave the right to become children of God" (John 1:12), "we are now children of God" (1 John 3:2); Romans 8:16 has "we are God's children".
rows.different: In John 1:12 it is a right given "to all who did receive Him"; in 1 John 3:1 it is a name, "that we should be called children of God", and "that is what we are!"; Romans 9:8 sets "the children of the flesh" beside "the children of the promise"; John 11:52 speaks of "the scattered children of God", "to gather them together into one". 1 John 3:10 sets "the children of God" beside "the children of the devil".

rows.title: Sons of God; sons of the LORD your God

The Law & history: Genesis 6:4
the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men
Deuteronomy 14:1
You are sons of the LORD your God
Psalms & wisdom: Job 2:1
the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD
Gospels & Acts: since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God
The letters: the revelation of the sons of God
You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus

rows.alike: Each names some "sons of God", or in Deuteronomy "sons of the LORD your God"; Deuteronomy 14:1 and Galatians 3:26 both say it to their hearers: "You are sons", "You are all sons".
rows.different: In Genesis the sons of God are set beside "the daughters of men", and in Job they "came to present themselves before the LORD", "and Satan also came with them"; Luke 20:36 says those of the resurrection "are like the angels" and "are sons of God"; Galatians 3:26 adds "through faith in Christ Jesus", and Romans 8:19 speaks of "the revelation of the sons of God" that the creation waits for.

rows.title: Sons of the Most High; "You are gods"

Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 82:6
You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High
Gospels & Acts: Is it not written in your Law
I have said you are gods
you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked
that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good

rows.alike: Psalm 82:6 and Luke 6:35 share the words "sons of the Most High", and Matthew 5:45 has "sons of your Father in heaven"; John 10:34 repeats the psalm's "I have said you are gods".
rows.different: The psalm states it, "You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High"; in Luke and Matthew it follows a command, "love your enemies", and the reason given is that "He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked" and sends His sun "on the evil and the good"; John cites the psalm as "written in your Law".

rows.title: Born of God

Gospels & Acts: children born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God
The letters: everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him
Anyone born of God refuses to practice sin, because God's seed abides in him
Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God
everyone born of God overcomes the world
anyone born of God does not keep on sinning

rows.alike: John's Gospel and 1 John use the same words, "born of God" (John 1:13; 1 John 3:9, 4:7, 5:1, 5:4).
rows.different: John 1:13 says what the birth is not: "not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man"; 1 John says what goes with it: one who "practices righteousness", "loves", "believes that Jesus is the Christ", "overcomes the world", and "refuses to practice sin".

rows.title: Born again; the God who gave you birth

The Law & history: Deuteronomy 32:18
you forgot the God who gave you birth
Gospels & Acts: no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again
The letters: through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit
He chose to give us birth through the word of truth
He has given us new birth into a living hope
you have been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God

rows.alike: God is the one who gives birth: "the God who gave you birth" (Deuteronomy 32:18), "He chose to give us birth" (James 1:18), "He has given us new birth" (1 Peter 1:3); John 3:3 and 1 Peter 1:23 share "born again".
rows.different: Deuteronomy says "you forgot the God who gave you birth"; in John it is a condition, "unless he is born again"; James and 1 Peter name the means as "the word of truth" and "the living and enduring word of God", 1 Peter 1:3 "the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead", and Titus 3:5 "the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit".

rows.title: Heirs

The Law & history: Genesis 15:3
a servant in my household will be my heir
Genesis 15:4
one who comes from your own body will be your heir
The Prophets: heirs from Judah; My elect will possess My mountains
The letters: the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world
if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless
if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ
you are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise
as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave
we would become heirs with the hope of eternal life
His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things
became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith
Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise
fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life

rows.alike: The word is "heir" throughout, and several tie it to Abraham and a promise: "your heir" (Genesis 15:4), "heir of the world" (Romans 4:13), "heirs according to the promise" (Galatians 3:29), "heirs of the promise" (Hebrews 6:17).
rows.different: Genesis 15:4 says "one who comes from your own body"; Isaiah 65:9 "heirs from Judah"; Romans 8:17 joins heirs to children, "if we are children, then we are heirs"; Ephesians 3:6 says "the Gentiles are fellow heirs"; Hebrews 1:2 speaks of "His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things"; and what is inherited differs: "the world", "eternal life", "the gracious gift of life", "all things".

rows.title: Abba, Father

Gospels & Acts: all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.
The letters: God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”

rows.alike: Both have the same two words, "Abba, Father".
rows.different: In Mark 14:36 the words come with "Take this cup from Me"; in Galatians 4:6 it is "the Spirit of His Son" in "our hearts" that is "crying out", "because you are sons".

rows.title: You are our Father; call Me ‘Father'

The Law & history: Deuteronomy 32:6
Is He not your Father and Creator?
The Prophets: O LORD, You are our Father; we are the clay, and You are the potter
Have you not just called to Me, ‘My Father, You are my friend from youth.
I thought you would call Me ‘Father' and never turn away from following Me
A son honors his father, and a servant his master. But if I am a father, where is My honor?
Gospels & Acts: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name
The letters: Since you call on a Father who judges each one's work impartially

rows.alike: God is named or called on as Father: "You are our Father" (Isaiah 64:8), "call Me 'Father'" (Jeremiah 3:19), "Our Father in heaven" (Matthew 6:9), "you call on a Father" (1 Peter 1:17).
rows.different: In Deuteronomy, Jeremiah and Malachi it comes with a question or a lament against those spoken to: "Is this how you repay the LORD", "never turn away from following Me", and, to "you priests", "where is My honor?"; in Isaiah it is the people's own plea, "we are the clay"; in Matthew and Luke it is how to pray; 1 Peter adds that this Father "judges each one's work impartially".

rows.title: He will be My son, and I will be his Father

The Law & history: 1 Chronicles 22:10
He will be My son, and I will be his Father
1 Chronicles 28:6
for I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 89:26
He will call to Me, ‘You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation.'

rows.alike: God speaks of a son and of Himself as his Father: "He will be My son, and I will be his Father" (1 Chronicles 22:10), "I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father" (1 Chronicles 28:6); Psalm 89:26 has "He will call to Me, 'You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation.'"
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 28:6 names him, "Solomon your son", and 22:10 ties it to the house: "the one who will build a house for My Name"; Psalm 89:26 names no one in the verse, and has the words "You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation."

rows.title: My sons and My daughters

The Law & history: Deuteronomy 32:19
provoked to anger by His sons and daughters
The Prophets: Bring My sons from afar, and My daughters from the ends of the earth

rows.alike: Both speak of the LORD's sons and daughters: "His sons and daughters" (Deuteronomy 32:19), "My sons from afar, and My daughters from the ends of the earth" (Isaiah 43:6).
rows.different: In Deuteronomy the LORD "rejected them, provoked to anger by His sons and daughters"; in Isaiah He calls for them to be brought "from afar" and "from the ends of the earth".

rows.title: My son; My firstborn

The Law & history: Exodus 4:23
let My son go so that he may worship Me
The Prophets: For I am Israel's Father, and Ephraim is My firstborn

rows.alike: The speaker says "My son" and "My firstborn": "let My son go so that he may worship Me" (Exodus 4:23), "Ephraim is My firstborn" (Jeremiah 31:9).
rows.different: Exodus 4:23 ends with a threat, "I will kill your firstborn son!"; Jeremiah 31:9 is a promise to those who "come with weeping", and adds "I am Israel's Father".

rows.title: Discipline your son; the rod

The Law & history: 2 Samuel 7:14
When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 89:30
If his sons forsake My law
Psalm 89:32
I will attend to their transgression with the rod
Proverbs 13:24
He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently
Proverbs 19:18
Discipline your son, for in that there is hope
Proverbs 22:15
the rod of discipline drives it far from him
Proverbs 23:13
Do not withhold discipline from a child
Proverbs 29:17
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest
The letters: If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons
we have all had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?
Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good

rows.alike: A son is disciplined, often "with the rod": "I will discipline him with the rod of men" (2 Samuel 7:14), "He who spares the rod hates his son" (Proverbs 13:24), "earthly fathers who disciplined us" (Hebrews 12:9).
rows.different: In 2 Samuel and Psalm 89 it is God who will discipline, "him" and "his sons"; Proverbs speaks to a father, "Discipline your son", and does not name God; Hebrews sets "earthly fathers" beside "the Father of our spirits" and says lack of discipline means "not true sons".

rows.title: A father of the fatherless

The Law & history: Deuteronomy 10:18
He executes justice for the fatherless and widow
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 10:14
You are the helper of the fatherless
Psalm 10:18
to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed
Psalm 68:5
A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation
Psalm 146:9
He sustains the fatherless and the widow
The Prophets: in You the fatherless find compassion
Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives
Gospels & Acts: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you

rows.alike: The fatherless are named with God as the one who acts for them: "A father of the fatherless" (Psalm 68:5), "the helper of the fatherless" (Psalm 10:14), "He sustains the fatherless" (Psalm 146:9); several add "the widow".
rows.different: Only Psalm 68:5 calls God "A father" of them; Hosea 14:3 has "in You the fatherless find compassion"; Jeremiah 49:11 has "Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives"; John 14:18 has "I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you".

rows.title: Rebellious children; a perverse and crooked generation

The Law & history: Deuteronomy 32:5
the blemish on them is not that of His children, but of a perverse and crooked generation
Deuteronomy 32:20
they are a perverse generation-children of unfaithfulness
The Prophets: I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me
deceitful children, children unwilling to obey the LORD's instruction
They are surely My people, sons who will not be disloyal
They are foolish children, without understanding
But the children rebelled against Me
The letters: children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation

rows.alike: The word "children" is used of those who turn from God: "they have rebelled against Me" (Isaiah 1:2), "rebellious children" (Isaiah 30:1), "faithless children" (Jeremiah 3:14); and Deuteronomy 32:5 and Philippians 2:15 share the words "perverse and crooked generation" / "crooked and perverse generation".
rows.different: Deuteronomy 32:5 says the blemish "is not that of His children"; Isaiah 63:8 has God saying "sons who will not be disloyal"; Jeremiah calls them to "Return"; in Philippians 2:15 the generation is the one in which the hearers are to be "children of God without fault".

rows.title: Children of God and children of the devil

Gospels & Acts: Our only Father is God Himself
If God were your Father, you would love Me
You belong to your father, the devil
the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one
O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness
The letters: By this the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil

rows.alike: Each speaks of being the child of God or of the devil, the evil one: "You are doing the works of your father" (John 8:41), "the sons of the evil one" (Matthew 13:38), "child of the devil" (Acts 13:10), "the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil" (1 John 3:10).
rows.different: In John 8 the hearers say "Our only Father is God Himself" and Jesus answers "If God were your Father, you would love Me"; Matthew 13:38 is the explanation of a parable, "the good seed" and "The weeds"; Acts 13:10 is said to one man; 1 John 3:10 gives the test: "Anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God".

rows.title: Sons of light, children of light

Gospels & Acts: the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light
believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light
The letters: you are all sons of the light and sons of the day

rows.alike: The same wording: "sons of light" (Luke 16:8, John 12:36), "sons of the light" (1 Thessalonians 5:5) and "children of light" (Ephesians 5:8).
rows.different: John 12:36 says how to "become sons of light": "believe in the Light"; Ephesians 5:8 says "you were once darkness"; Luke 16:8 sets them beside "the sons of this age"; 1 Thessalonians 5:5 adds "sons of the day".

rows.title: Carried, as a man carries his son

The Law & history: Exodus 19:4
how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to Myself
Deuteronomy 1:31
the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son
The Prophets: who have been sustained from the womb, carried along since birth
I have made you, and I will carry you
He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old

rows.alike: The LORD "carried" His people: "carried you" (Exodus 19:4; Deuteronomy 1:31), "carried along since birth" (Isaiah 46:3), "carried them all the days of old" (Isaiah 63:9).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 1:31 gives the likeness "as a man carries his son", and Exodus 19:4 "on eagles' wings"; Deuteronomy speaks of "the wilderness", Isaiah 46 of "from the womb" and "to your old age".
